summary: This Wikipedia-sourced note covers several aspects of Cyprus: language use (Greek and Turkish as official languages, English widely spoken), water supply (dams and desalination plants), Ottoman-era governance and the Church of Cyprus, local broadcasting, post-1974 politics and the population of Northern Cyprus according to the 2006 census, and the island's climate. It is a collection of excerpts rather than a single narrative.
one_line: Overview of Cyprus covering languages, water supply, Ottoman-era governance, broadcasting, 1974 politics, population and climate.
key_facts: Cyprus has two official languages, Greek and Turkish, with Armenian and Cypriot Maronite Arabic recognised as minority languages.
English was the sole official language during British colonial rule and the lingua franca until 1960.
English continued to be used de facto in courts of law until 1989 and in legislation until 1996.
80.4% of Cypriots are proficient in English as a second language.
Cyprus has a total of 107 dams (plus one currently under construction) and reservoirs with a total water storage capacity of about 330,000,000 m3.
Water desalination plants have supplied almost 50 per cent of domestic water in Cyprus since 2001.
The Ottomans applied the millet system to Cyprus, under which non-Muslim peoples were governed by their own religious authorities.
Ottoman rule of Cyprus was at times indifferent and at times oppressive, and the island began over 250 years of economic decline.
The Cyprus Broadcasting Corporation is the state-owned broadcaster and runs two television channels.
BRT is the Turkish Cypriot equivalent to the Cyprus Broadcasting Corporation in Northern Cyprus.
Around 150,000 settlers from Turkey are believed to be living in the north of Cyprus.
The 2006 census carried out by Northern Cyprus counted 256,644 (de jure) people living in Northern Cyprus.
Of the 256,644 people in Northern Cyprus in the 2006 census, 27,333 were born in Turkey and 2,482 were born in the UK.
Average annual coastal temperatures are around 24 °C (75 °F) during the day and 14 °C (57 °F) at night.
Summers in Cyprus last about eight months, beginning in April and ending in November.
